title: Recover transient request failures
summary: Retry safe operations after transient failures, within the existing deadline. The proposal adds upstream calls; operation safety and load tolerance need validation.

context.problem: In this illustrative scenario, a brief upstream failure immediately ends a request even when another attempt could succeed.
context.baseline: Hypothetical current behavior: the request service makes one upstream attempt and returns its result or error.
context.scope: Example proposal for evaluating the report format. No project code, implementation, or test results have been reviewed.
constraints: Preserve the response shape and overall deadline.
Retry only operations known to be safe to repeat.
assumptions: Failure classification and operation safety must be available from upstream contracts.
Example retry limits require workload validation.

visual.caption: The service makes one attempt; a transient failure ends the request.

edges.label: Current single upstream attempt
edges.issue: A short-lived upstream failure immediately ends the request. Even if a safe repeat could succeed, this baseline makes no second attempt.

changes.title: Introduce a bounded retry policy
changes.description: Add a policy inside the request service. A successful first attempt follows the existing path; an eligible transient failure can receive another attempt.
changes.why: Some short-lived failures may recover without requiring the client to submit a new request.

visual.caption: The initial attempt and response format stay the same. Recovery is added between an eligible failure and the final result.

before.label: Every failure immediately ends the request

after.label: Bounded retry policy
after.detail: Recover only when eligibility and remaining budget permit it.

changes.title: Make retry eligibility explicit
changes.description: Evaluate operation safety, failure classification, remaining attempts, and remaining time before scheduling another attempt. Permanent errors and ineligible operations return immediately.
changes.why: Recovery must not repeat unsafe work or consume an unbounded amount of time.

visual.caption: The new decision protects the existing return path. A retry loops back to another attempt only while every eligibility condition holds.

nodes.label: Retry allowed?
nodes.detail: Safe operation + transient error + attempt budget + time budget.

nodes.label: Wait within deadline
nodes.detail: Apply bounded backoff and jitter before the next attempt.

edges.label: Wait ends and time budget still permits an attempt

changes.title: Define limits and preserve the external contract
changes.description: Use an explicit attempt cap and bounded waits. Keep the original request deadline and response shape. These example values describe a proposal, not measured production settings.
changes.why: A small, visible policy is easier to reason about and tune than implicit recovery behavior.

visual.caption: Recovery settings change; externally visible response structure and the overall deadline remain the constraints.

rows.label: Total attempts
rows.after: At most 3, including the first attempt

rows.label: Wait between attempts
rows.after: 200 ms, then 400 ms, when the remaining deadline permits

changes.title: Record retry states for operational diagnosis
changes.description: Track attempting, waiting, and finished states with the attempt count. Record why recovery stopped without adding fields to the client response.
changes.why: Operators need to distinguish a permanent error from an exhausted retry budget when investigating failures.

visual.caption: Waiting is the new state. Completion includes a result or a recorded stop reason; another attempt always passes through the policy checks.

nodes.label: Finished
nodes.detail: Success, ineligible failure, or exhausted budget, with a recorded reason.

edges.label: Wait completes; budget permits another attempt
Success or retry policy declines recovery

manualChanges.action: Confirm and document which upstream operations are safe to repeat before enabling retries for them.
manualChanges.prerequisite: The relevant upstream operation contracts are available.
manualChanges.verification: Every enabled operation has an explicit safety rule; unknown operations remain ineligible.

manualChanges.action: Review the proposed attempt and waiting limits against the service deadline and representative upstream latency.
manualChanges.prerequisite: Representative request latency and the existing deadline are known.
manualChanges.verification: The selected settings preserve the overall deadline and have been exercised under transient failure.

impact.description: Some eligible transient failures may recover inside the original request. A successful first attempt keeps the existing behavior; no recovery rate is claimed without measurement.
Unsafe operations and permanent failures end immediately. Correct failure classification becomes a dependency of recovery behavior.
Eligible failures can produce additional upstream calls and waiting time. The policy caps total attempts and keeps recovery within the original deadline.
Operational records gain attempt counts and stop reasons. Client payloads remain unchanged; logging volume may increase for retried requests.

risks.title: Repeating an unsafe operation
risks.condition: An operation is incorrectly classified as safe to repeat, and its first attempt already performed a side effect.
risks.consequence: A retry can perform the side effect again.
risks.mitigation: Use an explicit eligibility rule for each operation and leave unknown operations ineligible. Verify safety with the upstream contract.

risks.title: Amplifying an upstream outage
risks.condition: Many concurrent requests encounter the same transient failure and become eligible to retry.
risks.consequence: Additional attempts can increase load on the upstream system while it is already unhealthy.
risks.mitigation: Keep the attempt cap and jitter, measure behavior under load, and revisit eligibility or limits if the upstream cannot tolerate the extra work.
